setup.title: Welcome to KremboNet
setup.intro: Two things to set up, then you are done. You can change both later.
setup.hubNameHint: Shown in the sidebar header and used as the subject prefix on alert email. Defaults to KremboNet.
setup.passwordHint: At least {{count}} characters. This is a single shared password for everyone who administers the hub — there are no user accounts.
setup.footnote: Add your printers from the admin portal once you are in. Nothing leaves your network — this hub talks to devices on your LAN and stores everything in a local file.

admin.title: Admin
admin.subtitle: Devices, access, alerts, appearance, and paper code mapping
admin.disabledBody: No admin password is set. Either complete first-run setup at <setup>, or set <env> in <file> and restart. A blank password disables the portal rather than leaving it open.

settings.name: Name
settings.nameHint: Shown in the sidebar and used as the subject prefix on alert email.
settings.subtitleHint: The line under the name. Leave blank to hide it entirely.
settings.logoHint: Shown in place of the name and subtitle. Paste a URL, or upload a file to embed it — embedding needs no web server, which is usually the easiest option on a LAN. SVG, PNG, JPG, WebP or GIF, up to {{limit}}KB encoded.
settings.logoEmbeddedHint: {{size}} stored in the database. Remove it to go back to a URL.
settings.logoTooBig: That image encodes to {{size}}KB, over the {{limit}}KB limit. Export it smaller — an SVG or a trimmed PNG is usually a few KB.
settings.logoWrongType: {{type}} is not an image format this accepts.
settings.logoUnreadable: The file could not be read.
settings.accessPublicHint: Anyone who can reach the hub on the network sees device status.
settings.accessPasscodeHint: Viewers enter a shared passcode once per browser.
settings.accessAdminHint: Only a signed-in administrator sees anything.
settings.viewerPasscodeKeep: Leave blank to keep the stored passcode.
settings.viewerPasscodeNew: Shared with viewers. Not the admin password — it grants read access only.
settings.viewerPasscodeClearHint: Only available while access is public or admins-only.
settings.accessFootnote: The admin portal is always reachable at <admin>, whatever this is set to — otherwise an admins-only hub could lock out the person who set it.
settings.themeKioskHint: Dark, larger text, no sidebar — for a wall display.
settings.languageHint: Applies to everyone who opens this hub.
settings.customCssHint: Appended after the built-in stylesheet, so these rules win. The palette is driven by custom properties on <root> — override those rather than restyling each component. <import> and remote <url> are stripped: this hub does not fetch anything off the local network.
settings.cssAdjusted: Your CSS was adjusted on save.
settings.smtpTlsHint: On for port 465. Leave off for 587, which upgrades via STARTTLS.
settings.smtpPasswordKeep: Leave blank to keep the stored password.
settings.smtpPasswordNew: For Google Workspace use an App Password, not the account password.
settings.testHint: Sends using the last saved settings, so save before testing.
settings.wasteThresholdHint: % full — this tank fills as the inks drain, so it alerts high
settings.hysteresisHint: How far past the threshold a supply must recover before the alert clears
settings.pollIntervalHint: minutes — how often ink and paper are read and alerts evaluated
settings.alertsEnabledHint: Turn off to keep polling without sending any mail.
settings.noCheckYet: No update check has completed yet.
settings.checkFailed: The last update check could not reach GitHub.
settings.updateCheckHint: Asks GitHub once a day whether a newer release exists. This is the only outbound connection the hub makes on its own — it sends nothing about this install, and it fails silently when blocked. Turn it off for an air-gapped deployment.

version.commandHint: Run it where <file> lives, after pulling the new source. Your <data> directory is untouched.

devices.title: Devices
devices.empty: No devices yet. Add one to start collecting readings.
devices.name: Name
devices.unknownAdapterTitle: No adapter is registered under this id
devices.enabledHint: Disabled devices are kept but never polled.
devices.betterMatch: looks like a better match than the selected adapter.
devices.secretStored: Leave blank to keep the stored value.
devices.suppressionHint: Silences notification, never monitoring. A muted device is still polled, still evaluated, and still shown as failing here — only the email and webhooks stop.
devices.maintenanceModeHint: Silences all alert rules for this printer while under physical service or testing. It is still polled and still shown as failing here — only the notifications stop.
devices.probeIpHint: Tests the address for IPP, SNMP and a web interface, then fills in the settings that worked.
devices.probeSnmpOnlyTip: This gives supply levels and status. Enable IPP on the device for live queue and paper tray tracking.
devices.probeHttpOnly: Answered on {{protocols}} only — a web interface, which this hub cannot poll. Enable IPP or SNMP on the device, then probe again.
devices.probeNothing: Nothing answered at that address. Check the printer is powered on and that the address is right.
devices.deleteBody: Are you sure you want to delete "{{name}}"? Its readings and supply history will be removed and cannot be recovered.
devices.probeUnidentified: Answered on {{protocols}}, but nothing this hub can poll identified itself. Check the device is a printer and that IPP or SNMP is enabled on it.

discover.title: Auto-discover
discover.intro: Sweeps a range of addresses for printers answering on IPP or SNMP and identifies what it finds.
discover.subnetHint: CIDR notation, /20 or smaller. Any address on the network works — <example> scans the whole /24 it sits on.
discover.communityHint: Only used to detect SNMP devices during the sweep. Devices using a different community will not answer and will not be found.
discover.inProgress: Connecting to every address in the range. This takes a few seconds.
discover.timedOut: The scan hit its time limit, so this list may be incomplete. Try a smaller range.
discover.truncated: More addresses answered than could be identified in one pass. The rest are not shown — add these, then scan again.
discover.nothingFound: Nothing answered on IPP (631) or SNMP (161). If you expected a device here, check that it is powered on, and that SNMP is enabled with the community string above.
discover.addByHandTitle: Nothing here identified itself as a supported device. Add it by hand if you know what it is.
discover.snmpOnlyTip: Provides supply & status telemetry. Enable IPP on device for live queue & paper tray tracking.

paperTypes.name: Name
paperTypes.unmappedHint: Unmapped codes appear on the device page as the raw code plus roll width, never as a guessed name.
paperTypes.discoveredHint: Codes your printers are reporting right now. Unmapped ones are listed first — give each a friendly name and it appears everywhere the code did.
paperTypes.discoveredEmpty: No paper codes have been reported yet. They appear here once a printer that loads coded media has been polled.
paperTypes.suggestTitle: A common name for this vendor code. It fills the field — check it matches the paper actually loaded before mapping it.
paperTypes.helpWhat: Printers report the loaded paper as an opaque code rather than a name — usually in reverse-domain form, like com.canon-012f. Neither IPP nor SNMP carries a human label alongside it, so the code is all this hub receives.
paperTypes.helpWhy: Manufacturers use their own codes because the paper catalogue is theirs: the same stock is a different product, with a different profile, on every brand of plotter. That is also why no list of codes ships with this hub — a table lifted from one office’s driver is wrong for the next one, so an unnamed code is shown as the raw code rather than a guess someone might plot a job on.
paperTypes.helpGlobal: Naming a code globally applies it to every printer that reports it, which is what makes the Media Catalog useful: two plotters loading the same stock group under one name instead of two codes. Map a code to a single device only when that machine genuinely uses it for something else.

alerts.activeEmpty: Nothing is past its threshold. Alerts fire once on crossing, so quiet is the normal state.
alerts.recentEmpty: No alerts have been generated yet.
alerts.subject: Subject
alerts.mutedNotice: {{name}} is in maintenance mode. The condition is still tracked and still shown here — only the email and webhooks stop.

alertRules.title: Alert rules
alertRules.intro: Alerting is opt-in. Each rule says what to watch, on which printers, and who to tell — and a hub with no rules sends nothing at all.
alertRules.emptyBody: Nothing will be emailed or posted to a webhook until you add one. Conditions are still detected, recorded on the activity log, and shown on the dashboard.
alertRules.emptyHint: Add a rule to start being told about the things this hub already notices.
alertRules.name: Rule name
alertRules.toggleAria: Turn the rule “{{name}}” on or off
alertRules.deleteBody: “{{name}}” will stop firing and cannot be recovered. Nothing else about your printers changes.

thresholdHint.offline: How long a printer must stay unreachable before this fires. Blank fires as soon as it is called offline.
thresholdHint.supply_low: Fires at or below this. Blank uses the hub threshold from Settings — the number that turns the bar red.
thresholdHint.waste_full: Fires at or above this. Blank uses the hub threshold from Settings.

alertRules.scopeAllHint: Every printer now registered, and any added later.
alertRules.noPrinters: No printers are registered yet. Add one under Admin → Devices.
alertRules.destinationsHint: A rule needs at least one destination. Without one it would match conditions and then do nothing.
alertRules.sendEmailHint: Uses the SMTP settings from the Settings tab.
alertRules.recipientsHint: Leave blank to use the global alert recipients. Addresses here replace that list for this rule rather than adding to it.
alertRules.webhooksHint: Configured under Alerts → Webhooks. Tick the ones this rule should post to.
alertRules.noWebhooks: No webhooks configured yet. Add one under Alerts → Webhooks.
alertRules.repeatHint: How often to say it again while the condition holds. It always stops when the condition clears.
alertRules.conditionHint: The rule fires when any one of these holds. Pick at least one.
alertRules.needCondition: Pick at least one condition for this rule to watch.

webhooks.title: Webhook destinations
webhooks.intro: Alerts go to every enabled destination as well as email. A destination that fails does not stop the others, and does not stop the mail.
webhooks.name: Name
webhooks.headersHint: JSON object. Used for things like an auth token on a private ntfy topic. Values are stored server-side and never sent back to this page — leave blank when editing to keep what is already there.
webhooks.enabledHint: Turn off to stop sending here without deleting the setup.

urlHints.discord: Channel → Edit Channel → Integrations → Webhooks → Copy Webhook URL.
urlHints.slack: A Slack Incoming Webhook URL, or the equivalent from Mattermost.
urlHints.ntfy: The full topic URL, e.g. https://ntfy.sh/my-plotter-alerts.
urlHints.generic: Any endpoint that accepts a JSON POST.

reset.title: Data & system reset
reset.intro: Each action removes what it names and nothing else. None can be undone.

activity.title: Clear activity log
activity.body: Deletes the event history. Devices, supplies, and settings are kept.
activity.confirmBody: Every recorded event is deleted. Your devices and settings are untouched. This cannot be undone.

devices.title: Clear printers
devices.body: Removes every registered printer and its readings. Settings are kept.
devices.confirmBody: Every printer, along with its supplies, media, and queue history, is deleted. Your settings stay. You will need to add printers again. This cannot be undone.

media.title: Reset media mappings
media.body: Reverts every paper-code name to the built-in defaults, discarding your edits.
media.confirmBody: All custom paper-code names and per-printer overrides are discarded and the factory defaults restored. This cannot be undone.

factory.title: Factory reset
factory.body: Erases everything — printers, settings, and your admin login — and returns the hub to first-run setup.
factory.confirmBody: Every printer, mapping, setting, and the admin password are erased. The hub returns to onboarding as if freshly installed, and you will be signed out immediately. This cannot be undone.
